clue.text: Small Australian songbird crossing northern horizon

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the singer's name is said to straddle the abbreviation, so it sits inside her

parts.note: Kylie Minogue, the Australian pop singer

explanation.surface: A little bird from Australia flies across a northern horizon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Songbird' is not a bird at all but the singer Kylie Minogue; 'crossing' puts N inside KYLIE, giving KYLINE after S.
explanation.definitionFit: The skyline is the line where land or buildings meet the sky, the visible horizon.

clue.text: Bill might get this Home Counties Tory fearful

parts.note: the Home Counties around London lie in the South East, abbreviated SE
CON is short for Conservative, a Tory
dreading means being fearful of something

explanation.surface: A frightened Conservative from the shires around London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' looks like a man's name; it is a parliamentary bill.
explanation.definitionFit: A parliamentary bill passes through a second reading, the main debate on its principles.

clue.text: Longed for money, finally obtained fair and square

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word money

parts.note: earned means gained honestly, by work

explanation.surface: Someone longed for money that was honestly earned.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long for something intensely, so the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Find Perth essentially dead

indicators.note: the essence of each word is its core, so each loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An instruction to discover that the Australian city is basically lifeless.
explanation.definitionFit: Inert means lifeless or motionless, so it can stand for dead.

clue.text: I must log out of game during, say, vespers

indicators.note: the trimmed meat sits during, that is within, the abbreviation

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is how 'say' introduces an instance

indicators.note: logging out means leaving, so the letter is taken out of the meat

parts.note: venison is deer meat, a classic game dish
the letter I itself

explanation.surface: A gamer must quit play in time for evening prayers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'log out of game' reads like a computer game; 'game' is the meat VENISON, which loses its I to give VENSON inside EG.
explanation.definitionFit: Vespers is the evening service of prayer, which the Anglican church calls evensong.

clue.text: Maybe Homer's gone out to chase one of his letters

indicators.note: one piece chasing another comes after it, so the scrambled word follows

parts.note: Homer wrote in Greek, and pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: out suggests the word gone is thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: The poet Homer has gone off chasing one of the letters of his alphabet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Homer' looks like the Greek poet, which suits 'his letters'; the definition reads it as a homing pigeon. 'out' rearranges GONE as GEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A homer is a homing pigeon, a bird bred to fly back to its loft, so 'maybe' marks an example.

clue.text: In pieces regularly after dad loses it

indicators.note: after places the picked letters behind the word for father

parts.note: pa is an informal word for dad

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the phrase in pieces

explanation.surface: Dad goes to pieces, again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'In pieces': N I C S.
explanation.definitionFit: To lose it is an idiom for losing self-control, the same as panicking.

clue.text: Appreciation of playing guitar with Ted

indicators.note: playing signals the letters being played with and rearranged

explanation.surface: Applause for Ted's guitar performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Gratitude is thankfulness, the appreciation felt for kindness received.

clue.text: Leave starter of most savoury layer of eggs

indicators.note: leave tells the solver to drop the opening letter of the next word

parts.note: rich food is heavy and full of flavour, savoury

explanation.surface: Skip the first course of most savoury egg dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'layer of eggs' looks like a stratum in a dish; it is a bird that lays eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The ostrich lays the largest eggs of any bird, so it is a layer of eggs.

clue.text: Julius invited to tea with Trotsky, a fickle person

indicators.note: the setter is invited along to tea, so he follows straight after it

parts.note: cha (or char) is British slang for tea
Julius is the setter's pseudonym, so the setter refers to himself as me
Leon Trotsky, the Russian revolutionary

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of being asked to tea with Trotsky, perhaps a turncoat.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter's own pseudonym in a clue usually stands for ME or I.
explanation.definitionFit: Like the lizard that changes colour, a chameleon is a person who changes opinions or loyalties to suit the company.

clue.text: Caper 14 (ignoring fast bits)

indicators.note: ignoring the bits means leaving those letters out of the cross-referenced word

parts.note: the answer to 14 down, which is fantastic
the letters of fast, taken here as pieces to be dropped

explanation.surface: A cross-reference asks for a caper with the quick parts skipped.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters F, A, S, T are removed one by one, in that order, from FANTASTIC, leaving A N T I C.
explanation.definitionFit: An antic is a playful or grotesque trick, the same kind of prank as a caper.

clue.text: Key to French Arsenal ace moving here for a bargain

parts.note: cle is the French word for key

indicators.note: moving signals the letters being shifted into a new order

explanation.surface: The key to a French player joining Arsenal is that the deal came cheap.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenal is a London football club; 'moving' suggests a transfer, but it rearranges ARSENAL ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A clearance sale sells off stock cheaply, the place to come for a bargain.

clue.text: Group without access to the web

parts.note: without means having no, so it gives no
the net is the internet, the way onto the web

explanation.surface: A group of people stuck offline, with no internet connection.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonet is a group of nine, usually musicians playing together.

clue.text: Offering to swap cars in the event of slippery roads?

indicators.note: swapping the letters of cars around rearranges them

parts.note: the word as written
if means in the event of, introducing a condition
ice is what makes roads slippery, standing in for them here

explanation.surface: A motoring tip: trade in your cars if the roads turn icy.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacrifice is something offered up, as to a god, so it is a kind of offering.

clue.text: Come up with a new word for "thin- sounding, slender"

definitions.text: Come up with a new word for

indicators.note: sounding means the word said aloud is spelt differently in the answer

parts.note: a reedy voice or tone is thin and high
fine means slender or thin, as in a fine thread

explanation.surface: A request to find a fresh term for something both reedy in tone and slim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thin-sounding' looks like one adjective for a reedy voice; it splits into 'thin' and the 'sounding' signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To redefine is to give a fresh meaning or description, the same as finding new words for something.

clue.text: Aficionado beginning to taste Italian wine cold — wonderful!

parts.note: an aficionado is a keen fan

indicators.note: beginning to takes the opening letter of taste

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling wine from Piedmont in Italy
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A wine lover samples chilled Italian wine and pronounces it great.
explanation.definitionFit: Fantastic is an exclamation of delight, a synonym of wonderful.

clue.text: Writer Thomas Hardy's first impressions given gold covers

indicators.note: the two forms of gold cover the initials by sitting on either side of them

parts.note: gold is both AU, its chemical symbol, and OR, its heraldic name, one placed at each side

indicators.note: the first impression of each name is its opening letter

explanation.surface: Novelist Thomas Hardy's early impressions are given a gilded cover.
explanation.walkthrough: Gold has two crossword forms, the chemical symbol and the heraldic tincture, so one goes on each side as the 'covers'.
explanation.definitionFit: An author is a writer, the person who wrote a book.

clue.text: A kind of rush to build Donegal Hospital at the start

indicators.note: at the start places the hospital letter before the rest

parts.note: H is the map sign for a hospital

indicators.note: building the place name means reassembling its letters

explanation.surface: Plans to construct a hospital in Donegal, an Irish county.
explanation.definitionFit: A headlong rush is a reckless dash, so headlong describes one kind of rush.

clue.text: Climb American Sierra a bit?

parts.note: Sierra is the code word for S in the NATO alphabet
a cent is a small coin, just a bit of a dollar

explanation.surface: Is this a bit of an American mountain range, perhaps one to climb?
explanation.definitionFit: An ascent is a climb, the act of going up a slope or mountain.

clue.text: Officer suitable to probe notorious murderer

indicators.note: probing means poking inside, so this word goes into the murderer

parts.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: A detective is fit to investigate an infamous killer.
explanation.definitionFit: A captain is a commissioned rank in the army and navy, so an officer.

clue.text: Big name in Italian fashion left for a time to become a comedian

indicators.note: left stands in for a time, replacing that letter

parts.note: Benetton, the Italian clothing company
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: An Italian fashion house briefly quits and turns into a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: One T in BENETTON becomes L. Ben Elton is a British stand-up comedian and writer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ben Elton is a well-known British comedian, so the name fits the description.

clue.text: Vehicle temperature about 11C, starts to apply brakes

parts.note: a. is an abbreviation for about, used before an approximate date
XI is 11 in Roman numerals

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: At about 11 degrees Celsius a driver begins to brake.
explanation.walkthrough: '11C' reads as a temperature but splits into XI and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A taxicab is a car for hire, one kind of vehicle.

clue.text: Don't press top Italian trousers

indicators.note: trousers is a verb here: the phrase pockets the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: Laundry advice: don't iron the top part of Italian trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trousers' looks like a noun for what is pressed; it is a verb, meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: Stop it is the command that tells someone not to do something, as does don't.

clue.text: Firmly established, as the boss of Gardener's World might describe himself?

definitions.meaning: firmly fixed or set in place

definitions.text: as the boss of Gardener's World might describe himself?
definitions.meaning: the editor (Ed) in charge of a plant programme introducing himself

explanation.surface: The editor of a TV gardening show introduces himself as firmly rooted.
explanation.walkthrough: Gardener's World is a BBC gardening programme and magazine; its boss is the editor, ED, who might introduce himself as I'M PLANT ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implanted is fixed deeply in place, like a rooted idea, hence firmly established.

clue.text: Fairy daughter of the south replaced by papa

indicators.note: the daughter letter is swapped out and papa put in its place

parts.note: Dixie is a nickname for the southern states of the USA
Papa is the code word for P in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A Southern belle's fairy-tale role passes from the daughter to her father.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixie is a small mischievous sprite of folklore, one kind of fairy.

clue.text: Slate opening of terrible old theatre piece

parts.note: to pan or slate a show is to criticise it harshly

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of terrible

explanation.surface: Critics slam the opening night of a dreadful old play.
explanation.walkthrough: A panto (pantomime) is a British Christmas stage show for families.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantomime is a theatrical entertainment, a piece of theatre.

clue.text: Massive soldiers?

definitions.meaning: ... as an adjective means huge or massive
a GI is an American soldier, and a soldier ant is a kind of ant, so the question mark flags the play

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a pun: GI ANT is two kinds of soldier, the US infantryman and the soldier ant.
explanation.definitionFit: Giant as an adjective means enormous, the same idea as massive.

clue.text: Old country pub, one I renovated by Langley?

indicators.note: by means next to, so the agency follows directly

parts.note: PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: renovated suggests the letters of one are rebuilt in a new order

parts.note: Langley, Virginia, is the headquarters of the CIA

explanation.surface: A countryside pub has been done up by a builder called Langley.
explanation.walkthrough: Langley looks like a person's name; it is the Virginia town that stands for the CIA. 'renovated' rearranges ONE as OEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoenicia was an ancient land on the eastern Mediterranean coast, an old country of seafaring traders.

clue.text: Alas, no catering on board winter transport

indicators.note: the answer is carried on board the phrase, sitting within its letters

explanation.surface: A complaint that there is no food served aboard a winter vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A snocat is a tracked vehicle built for travelling over snow, so it is winter transport.

clue.text: Farewell item secured at the 10 did you say?

indicators.note: did you say marks a word heard rather than spelt as entered

parts.note: a bargain bought at a clearance sale (10 down) is a good buy

explanation.surface: A shopper asks whether a bargain was snapped up at the sale.
explanation.definitionFit: Goodbye is the word said on parting, a farewell.
